chunks: As for that which Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Kulayb al-Asadī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about al-naḥr, and he said: As for Minā, it is three days; and as for the towns, it is one day.

key_terms.النَّحْرِ: ritual slaughter, especially in the context of sacrificial rites
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, the sacred location associated with hajj rites
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the prescribed period in Minā
key_terms.فِي الْبُلْدَانِ: in the towns, meaning locations other than Minā
key_terms.يَوْمٌ وَاحِدٌ: one day, the prescribed period outside Minā

ai.seo_question: How many days are al-naḥr and slaughter observed in Minā and in other towns according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the days of al-naḥr and slaughter. It states that in Minā the period is three days, while in other towns it is one day, indicating a distinction in the ruling based on location during the rites of hajj.
